IRIS National Fair.source: IRIS submission guidelines + current portal; IRIS does not publish a simple public judging weight table.

stage_help.idea: Problem, prior work, research gap, hypothesis/question, proposed contribution and why it may be new.
stage_help.methodology: Variables, controls/comparators, sample/data, protocol, metrics, statistical/analytical plan, ethics/safety, resources and failure modes.
stage_help.submission: Paste the student-authored IRIS submission content: abstract, introduction/objective, innovation, methodology, results/conclusions and references. The engine also checks video/readiness requirements.

IRIS National Fair.rules: Original research/innovation, not display-only work. Current portal and annual guidelines control. Submission/video anonymity and current research-age/rules must be checked.

Regeneron ISEF.source: Society for Science Grand Award Judging Criteria, 2027 International Rules.

stage_help.idea: Research question/problem, gap, hypothesis/design goal, novelty and potential impact.
stage_help.methodology: Research plan, controls, sample/data, analysis, risk assessment, approvals/forms, regulated research issues and reproducibility.
stage_help.submission: Results, analysis, limitations, abstract/poster narrative and evidence that the student can defend the work in depth.

Regeneron ISEF.rules: Cannot apply directly; affiliated-fair route. Annual ISEF rules/forms and pre-approvals can be gating requirements.

RSI at MIT.source: CEE RSI materials: holistic review; complete essays, recommendations, transcript and available testing; prior research helpful but not required.

stage_help.profile: Grade, rigorous STEM coursework, scores if available, olympiads/competitions, research exposure, independent learning, leadership and intellectual interests.
stage_help.application: Evidence behind the profile: research role, outputs, distinctions, depth of subject engagement, activities, community contribution and recommenders.
stage_help.submission: Paste student-authored essay drafts/answers or summaries, recommender context, transcript/GPA context and final application evidence. The engine critiques alignment and gaps; it does not rewrite restricted student work.

RSI at MIT.rules: RSI selects the student, not a single project. Do not score it as a science-fair project. Use current CEE application instructions for cycle-specific eligibility/deadlines.

Conrad Challenge.source: Conrad Innovation Stage scoring guide (stage-specific; current-cycle guide must be reconfirmed).

stage_help.idea: Problem, customer/user, proposed innovation, existing alternatives, differentiation, IP/defensibility and potential impact.
stage_help.validation: Prototype status, technical feasibility, user/customer evidence, market sizing, business model, implementation, testing and iteration.
stage_help.submission: Innovation brief/materials, pitch/video narrative, evidence, team roles, defensibility and current stage deliverables.

Conrad Challenge.rules: Competition is stage-based. Apply the rubric for the actual stage/cycle, not one generic research rubric.

The Earth Prize.source: Official programme/submission materials; public percentage weights may not be published for every cycle.

stage_help.idea: Environmental problem, evidence of need, affected ecosystem/community, proposed solution and differentiation.
stage_help.validation: Prototype/pilot, impact metrics, baseline/comparator, stakeholder testing, implementation, financial/resource feasibility, longevity and risks.
stage_help.submission: Paste the current application/submission answers and evidence; the engine maps them to impact, innovation, feasibility, stakeholders, longevity and communication.

The Earth Prize.rules: Environmental sustainability relevance is a hard fit gate. Current annual submission questions control.

Stockholm Junior Water Prize.source: SIWI international criteria: relevance/significance, creativity, methodology/subject knowledge, practical skills, report and presentation.

stage_help.idea: Water challenge, scientific/social relevance, research question or design objective, existing approaches and proposed innovation.
stage_help.methodology: Scientifically accepted methods, experiments/monitoring, controls/comparators, data, analysis, practical execution and limitations.
stage_help.submission: Written report, abstract, essential results, impact, support received, poster/presentation narrative and defence readiness.

Stockholm Junior Water Prize.rules: International entry is through a participating country's national organiser; national rules/deadlines can differ.

Diamond Challenge.source: Diamond Challenge current-cycle rules/submission materials; no simple public percentage table should be invented.

stage_help.idea: Problem, customer/beneficiary, solution, unique value proposition, alternatives and why this venture matters.
stage_help.validation: Interviews/testing, prototype/MVP, traction, economics or sustainability model, channels, partners, risks and iteration.
stage_help.submission: Concept document, video/pitch content, evidence of traction, team capability and Q&A readiness.

Diamond Challenge.rules: Business Innovation and Social Innovation need different evidence emphasis; current rules and revenue cap must be checked.

Blue Ocean Competition.source: Official scoring criteria: Value Innovation 20%, Impact 20%, Technical Feasibility 20%, Commercial Viability & Scalability 20%, Presentation/Blue Ocean Tools 20%.

stage_help.idea: Problem/market, concept, differentiation, low-cost/value logic, target noncustomers and technical feasibility.
stage_help.strategy: Strategy Canvas, Three Tiers of Noncustomers, ERRC Grid, market potential, business model, feasibility and scale evidence.
stage_help.submission: Pitch transcript/storyboard plus required Blue Ocean tools. The engine checks clarity, evidence and alignment with the published five-part rubric.

Blue Ocean Competition.rules: Use of specified Blue Ocean tools is mandatory in the published competition instructions.

Technovation Girls.source: 2026–27 division-specific official rubrics; 1–5 scoring per item, with different Beginner/Junior/Senior requirements.

stage_help.idea: Community problem, affected users, evidence/sources, ethical issues, proposed digital solution, alternatives and technology choice.
stage_help.build: Working features, user tests, metrics, debugging, iterations, user feedback, adoption plan, business/financial logic and AI/tool transparency.
stage_help.submission: Paste the correct division's project description, pitch/technical video scripts, adoption plan and learning journey. Grade/age determines rubric.

Technovation Girls.rules: Division-specific rubric is mandatory; do not apply one generic weight table across ages.

Diana Award.source: Diana Award five criteria: Vision, Social Impact, Inspiring Others, Youth Leadership, Service Journey; retrospective professional nomination.

stage_help.impact: Describe the cause, why the young person acted, duration, role, beneficiaries, leadership and how the initiative evolved.
stage_help.evidence: Measured outcomes, beneficiary evidence, partnerships, independent validation, testimonials, reach, sustained service and evidence of inspiring others.
stage_help.submission: Paste the nomination evidence/answers and nominator context. The engine checks the five published dimensions and whether claims are evidenced and sustained.

Diana Award.rules: Retrospective award: do not treat it as a project competition or suggest starting a short-term project merely to win an award.

GSL Global Goals Competition.source: Official 2026–27 competition page and final submission criteria; final report max 1,000 words + digital submission, detailed judge weights not fully public.

stage_help.idea: SDG, community need, baseline understanding, team plan, intended beneficiaries, partners and realistic six-month action.
stage_help.impact: Activities delivered, baseline vs outcome measures, beneficiaries, hours, learning, partnerships, sustainability, challenges and adaptations.
stage_help.submission: Paste the final report (up to 1,000 words) and digital-submission script/summary. The engine maps evidence to official judging themes.

GSL Global Goals Competition.rules: Current participation requires GSL Member School route; 2026–27 dates and handbook govern.

Global Student Prize.source: Published judging dimensions include academic achievement, peer impact, wider impact, overcoming odds, creativity/innovation and global citizenship; official percentage weights not public.

stage_help.profile: Academics, major initiatives, peer/community impact, innovation, leadership, global citizenship and context.
stage_help.evidence: Measured outcomes, third-party validation, beneficiary evidence, scale/depth, sustained contribution, awards/media only where relevant and authentic role.
stage_help.submission: Paste application/nomination answers or structured evidence. The engine tests the profile against the published dimensions without inventing official weights.

Global Student Prize.rules: This validates an overall student profile, not one project. Annual eligibility/window must be confirmed.
